title: Harmony
hook: beauty that balances love and strength

segments.voice: Yesterday, Chesed and Gevurah: the river and its banks, Abraham's open tent and Isaac's awe. Your line was love and limits. In which conversation did you add a little of the other? Day one thousand one hundred seventy-eight.

A guitar string tuned too loose just flaps and buzzes. Tuned too tight, it snaps. Somewhere between, there's a point where it rings, and you can hear the moment it arrives. That point isn't half loose and half tight. It's something else entirely: a note. Yesterday left love and limits pulling in two directions, right arm and left arm. The kabbalists didn't leave them there. They put a third light in the middle, and they didn't call it compromise, or average, or fairness. They called it beauty. Today's word.
screen: `TOO LOOSE, IT BUZZES.` → `TOO TIGHT, IT SNAPS.` → `BETWEEN, IT RINGS.`

segments.voice: Tiferet. Beauty, glory, harmony. Turn it four ways. First, where it sits. On the kabbalists' map, Tiferet stands in the center, below Chesed and Gevurah, holding them together. Some teachers draw the whole tree in three columns: love on the right, strength on the left, and a middle column running straight down through Tiferet. Second, you've already heard it. Three days ago, in David's blessing: "the greatness, and the power, and the glory." That word glory, in Hebrew, is tiferet. It was in the list all along. Third, its face. Yesterday, Micah's line gave "the mercy to Abraham". The same verse begins with "the truth to Jacob". Kabbalists link Jacob to Tiferet, and Tiferet to truth: the son of Isaac and the grandson of Abraham, holding both inheritances in one life. Truth, in this picture, isn't harsh and isn't soft. It's what you get when love and strength are both honest. Fourth, the surprise. Harmony here is not the absence of tension. A chord has notes that differ. A face is beautiful partly because its features aren't all the same. Tiferet keeps Chesed and Gevurah both fully alive and lets them sound together. That's why the kabbalists didn't call it the middle. They called it beauty. Some teachers also call Tiferet the heart of the map, the place where the lights meet before they flow on, down toward the world. Tomorrow, where that flow goes next.
screen: `THE CENTER OF THE MAP.` · `GLORY, IN DAVID'S BLESSING.` · `JACOB, AND TRUTH.` · `NOT HALF AND HALF: A CHORD.` · then, large: `HARMONY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: find one balance. Settle, and breathe. Let your breath be the string. Breathe in a little too long, and notice the strain. Breathe out a little too short, and notice the rush. Then let it find the length where it rings, not forced either way. Stay there for a while. Now bring to mind one part of your life that's out of tune, too loose or too tight. Don't fix it. Just ask what the note would sound like if both sides were honest. The bell holds the time.
Tiferet. Beauty and harmony: the center of the sefirot, holding love and strength together, linked to Jacob and to truth. Today's word.
Your line: harmony. Today, when two good things pull at you, look for the note where both can sound, instead of picking a side. Day one thousand one hundred seventy-eight.

howItsDone: In Kabbalah, Tiferet is taught as the central sefirah that harmonizes Chesed and Gevurah; Hasidic teaching applies it to a balanced heart, often through the figure of Jacob.
